subtype: Coming of age and body changes [Receiver]
passage:
Dear Sabiha Khala,
Thank you for calling after Ammi told you about my first period. Before that week I felt so strange. Dadi said I mustn't touch the pickle jars and must never let Asif Bhai know, and I started hiding my pads in my school bag. I felt dirty, and also oddly important, like everyone was suddenly watching me grow up.
You told me it's a normal, healthy part of growing up, nothing unclean, and nothing to be ashamed of. You said faith has its own rules about prayer, and that is different from shame. Then you talked to Ammi. Now she keeps supplies openly in the bathroom cupboard, and yesterday even Asif Bhai just asked if I wanted a hot water bottle.
Love,
Rukhsar

qa.q: Where does Ammi keep supplies now?
What did Rukhsar feel in the week before Khala's call?
qa.a: Rukhsar felt ashamed and 'dirty', hiding pads, yet also oddly important, as if suddenly grown up and watched.

qa.q: What did Khala's call change, and why did it help?
qa.a: Khala gave simple facts, said periods are nothing unclean or shameful, separated faith rules from shame, and spoke to Ammi, so secrecy gave way to openness.

qa.q: How does Asif Bhai seem to see it now?
qa.a: Asif Bhai seems to treat it as ordinary, kindly offering a hot water bottle instead of it being a secret.

grounding: Shows a girl told to follow restrictions and keep secrecy after her first period, who feels both shamed and important until health facts and respect replace the stigma.

subtype: Coming of age and body changes [Receiver]
passage: Kaveri, seventeen, leans toward the school radio mic as Imran, the student host, nods for her to begin. 'When I was twelve, my family held a big coming-of-age function for me. Silk sari, relatives, photos, gifts. I felt like a queen, and also like everyone was staring at my body. For months after, during my periods, I sat on a separate mat and couldn't enter the puja room. My little brother Jeevan asked if I was sick. I didn't know what to say. Then our biology teacher explained periods plainly, no whispering, and Amma came to the parents' session too. Now at home we talk normally. Amma still keeps some customs, and I keep some because I choose to. But nobody calls me unclean.'

qa.a: Jeevan asked if Kaveri was sick.

qa.q: What did Kaveri feel at the coming-of-age function?
qa.a: Kaveri felt special, 'like a queen', but also embarrassed and self-conscious, as if everyone were staring at her body.

qa.q: What helped replace secrecy in Kaveri's home?
qa.a: A biology teacher explaining periods plainly, and Amma attending the parents' session, so the family could talk openly while choosing which customs to keep.

qa.q: How might Jeevan's understanding change now that the family talks openly?
qa.a: Jeevan would learn that periods are normal, not an illness, and could be more at ease and supportive instead of confused.

grounding: Illustrates a girl whose first period brings a celebration and restrictions that make her feel both important and shamed, until plain health facts and respect replace secrecy.
